q-11322.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14200038/assets/9c092436e6f2f66cd2ade33818209f001d1481f962c086da09c284975af83795.png)

Given the above sample space, find $P({X}^{′}).$
q-11322.worked_solution:
The Venn diagram tells us that $P(X)=\frac{2}{5}.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P({X}^{′}) & =1-P(X) \\  & =1-\frac{2}{5} \\  & =\frac{3}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-84440.name: Question 3
q-84440.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14200038/assets/5245725446c23cc37e5ca4ad5b4def939c1544100eb3488092f59c4ed0f8beaa.png)

Consider the sample space $S$ with the Venn diagram given above. What is $P(A)?$
q-84440.worked_solution:
From the given Venn diagram, we have $P(A)=y$ and $P({A}^{′})=\frac{y}{22}.$
Therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}P(A)+P({A}^{′}) & =1 \\ y+\frac{y}{22} & =1 \\ \frac{23y}{22} & =1 \\ y & =\frac{22}{23}.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently,  $P(A)=y=\frac{22}{23}.$
